title: Pancreatic Cancer: First Patients Treated in RASolute 309 Phase 3
description: Revolution Medicines began treating patients in RASolute 309, a Phase 3 trial of daraxonrasib plus zoldonrasib as first treatment for RAS G12D pancreatic cancer
summary: Revolution Medicines announced on October 5, 2026 that it has begun treating patients in RASolute 309, a global Phase 3 trial comparing daraxonrasib plus zoldonrasib with standard chemotherapy as first treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer with a RAS G12D change. No results exist yet, and the combination is not approved. This is a trial start, not a treatment result.

p: Revolution Medicines said it has begun treating patients in RASolute 309 (NCT07805954), a global, randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial. It enrolls adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma that carries the RAS G12D change and who have not been treated before.

sections.h: How the trial is set up
p: One group gets daraxonrasib (brand name Rasonque) plus zoldonrasib. The other gets gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, a standard chemotherapy pairing. The main goals are progression-free survival (time without the cancer growing) and overall survival.

According to the company, daraxonrasib is FDA-approved for previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer. Zoldonrasib is still investigational, and the combination as a first treatment is only under study. The company calls RASolute 309 the first Phase 3 study of a RAS(ON) inhibitor doublet.

The company says RAS G12D occurs in about 40% of pancreatic cancers and that five-year survival for metastatic disease is about 3%. A trial start is a step toward an answer, not an answer: no efficacy results from RASolute 309 have been reported, and the announcement is a company release.

faq.q: Is there a new pancreatic cancer treatment available from this trial?
faq.a: Not from this trial. The combination is under study and has no results yet. People interested in trials can ask their care team about eligibility.

faq.q: What is RAS G12D pancreatic cancer?
faq.a: It is pancreatic cancer whose tumor cells carry a specific change in the RAS gene. Revolution Medicines says about 40% of pancreatic cancers have it.
